newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn at parliament ctee July 21, audit day.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn at parliament ctee July 21, audit day.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn will meet the National Assembly finance committee on July 21 before presentation the same day of a crucial audit on France's public finances, committee head Henri Emmanuelli said on Wednesday.
Emmanuelli was speaking to reporters after Strauss-Kahn had met the committee in a closed-door session, his first since the new left-wing government took power a month ago.
Strauss-Kahn said last month the audit would be completed by July 21 and that it would be made public immediately.
A finance ministry source confirmed this plan on Wednesday and said: "the figures which will come out of the audit will be the ones that count."

The audit, commissioned by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, is expected to give a concrete indication on the state of public finances after a recent declarations by Strauss-Kahn that the 1997 deficit would not be limited to three percent of GDP, as would be required by those who advocate a rigid reading of the Maastricht treaty on monetary union.
A Government source said last Friday "first signs" showed the deficit heading for a "little beyond 3.4 or 3.5 percent."
